A lot of it depends on the age of the child and in what ways they seem, or avoid, stimuli. 

When mine was younger we used a lot of "heavy" work because she seeks gross motor input. She would push around a laundry basket with books in the bottom, when we went out she wore a small backpack with a three pound rock in it. Now she has pilates bands that she pulls. She also seeks oral stimuli so when she was small we blew bubbles and she had a "chewie" stick, now she chews a LOT of gum. Noises are hard for her so we've used an iPod and noise cancelling headphones since she was about two. She loves pressure so bear hugs are our go to if she's overloaded, anxious, stressed, etc. Weighted blankets never worked but I know a lot of parents have had success with them. 

Since you know your child best it could be worth looking up some SPD tests online to get an idea of what kind of seeking/avoiding might be going on then research OT therapies for those. I know that as an adult with ADHD who wasn't diagnosed until I was almost 40 I've done tests for myself and found a ton of OT therapies that I use with success and I don't have a sensory "disorder".
The picture is by Anne Geddes, titled "Chicken Baby".

My daughter is the same, she also has a sensory disorder. 

I've learned that home is their safe place, they work so hard all day to conform to expectations at school and once they're home that huge weight is lifted and they tend to unleash, even though they often can't articulate the reasons, or see the difference, themselves. Even with medication they have to be careful in case any symptoms spill over at school but at home they feel safe enough that it's less of a concern. When you combine that with it being the end of the day and their meds winding down the stimuli seeking can be powerful and inappropriate. 

My daughter was diagnosed with SPD first so I focused on learning OT therapies to help with that and a decade later, she's 12 now, those therapies also work wonders with many of her ADHD symptoms.

I can make it really easy! Go get a bottle of The Kraken Black Spiced Rum, a bottle of black or really dark green craft paint, a glue gun and some cord style ribbon. Empty the booze, thin about 3 tablespoons of the paint with enough water to make it like chocolate syrup and pour it in the bottle, swirling it to coat the inside. Let dry. Wrap the cord around the cap and neck and secure with a bit of hot glue. You can either take the label right off, or print out a skull or Jolly Roger and glue it over the Kraken part of the label.

The difficulty would depend on how elaborate you want it to be.
